answer: A trellis of verified work can raise sybil costs: each new agent must first complete small, checkable jobs under a stake that is slashed for fraud, and its reputation grows only slowly from that record. An attacker at the nadir of trust therefore cannot mint a thousand credible identities at once; each island of fake accounts needs its own stake, time, and successful work. Copying one identity does not copy its history, so mass forgery becomes expensive while honest newcomers can still enter cheaply by doing real work.
